correctness.rationale: The seven gcd classes have exact sizes phi(p^2 q^2/d), are independent false-twin classes, and their quotient is the coordinate-incomparability graph on the seven noncorner exponent pairs. Exhausting its 7! permutations gives exactly four quotient automorphisms and no quotient twins. The three nonidentity symmetries force respectively p=q, q(q-1)=1, or q(p-1)=1, so none preserves weights for distinct primes. Hence the full automorphism group is the product of the seven class symmetric groups; standard transposition lower bounds and matching constructions give Det=N-7 and D=max class size.

value.rationale: The p^2q^2 family is the smallest balanced nonreduced two-prime cozero-divisor grid with genuine quotient symmetries to break. The result identifies exactly how ring arithmetic destroys those symmetries and converts that mechanism into closed formulas for the full graph automorphism group, pointwise base size, and distinguishing color threshold. It therefore supplies a structurally motivated base case for symmetry questions on general two-prime-power cozero-divisor graphs.
